lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs beat the Islanders 4-2, moving to 9-14 on the season. They sit 13th in eastern conference, and the standings race sharpens a little every night. Before that, the club lost to the Blue Jackets 3-4. There is runway left in the schedule, and the work on rotations and matchups matters as much as the scoreboard. Next up: at Bruins on Fri 11/27 at 1:00 PM ET. The NHL calendar has flipped to building season - draft prep, trade talks, and the roster surgery that shapes the next contending window. For the Toronto Maple Leafs, the work runs from the draft table to the trade market, and the choices made this summer will define the next window.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The offseason finally has a pulse, and Toronto has supplied it - but one splash does not repair an entire roster. The Blue Jays agreed to a five-year, $80 million deal with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, a move that gives a rotation needing conviction a legitimate new centerpiece. Taira's 1.36 ERA and 141 strikeouts in 146 Pacific League innings explain the excitement, but his once-a-week workload also demands careful handling, perhaps even a six-man rotation. The finished season's -2.0 points are only useful now as a warning: Toronto cannot confuse activity with improvement. Valenzuela's 2027 role remains another unresolved piece, while the club still needs another impact starter and more relief help; interest in left-hander Adrian Morejon reportedly remains alive. Before the December 1 lockout deadline, watch whether Toronto turns Taira into the first move of a plan - or merely the first headline.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors are no longer merely waiting for better health; they are running out of runway. The 116-111 loss to Milwaukee on Nov. 23 dropped Toronto to a 1-game losing streak and seven losses in its last eight, leaving a 6-11 club fourth in the Atlantic Division and 8 games behind. Jakob Poeltl and Collin Murray-Boyles are preaching patience, but patience is a poor substitute for bodies in uniform: RJ Barrett remains sidelined by a right hamstring issue, while Kawhi Leonard deals with left knee swelling. Scottie Barnes' return offers a measure of stability, yet this roster has been fully healthy for only two games. Darko Rajakovic insists the team's standards remain high after his controversial praise of Milwaukee. Fine. Standards must now become results. Friday's 7:30 p.m. meeting with the Nets is the next test - and a chance to stop this slide before the standings make patience sound like denial.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders have stopped wobbling and started climbing - barely, but meaningfully. Washington's 22-20 victory over Cincinnati on Nov. 23 pushed the club to 4-5-1, second in the NFC East, and a two-game winning streak. That is not dominance; it is survival with teeth. Jayden Daniels now gets an intriguing new weapon in Brandon Aiyuk, who is joining the practice squad after the two repaired their relationship. "We've put the past behind us," Daniels said, and the timing matters with Terry McLaurin absent. Aiyuk is no instant cure - practice-squad players do not transform an offense by reputation - but his talent gives a team in need of juice a legitimate possibility. The margin remains thin, with Washington two games behind in the division. Sunday's 4:25 p.m. visit to Arizona is the next test: turn this streak into a trajectory, or reveal it as a brief reprieve.

the_latest.headline: Commanders beat Bengals 22-20
the_latest.dek: The walk-off victory keeps Washington's playoff hopes alive at 4-5-1 and marks its second straight comeback win in primetime. With the NFC East still within reach, the Commanders now carry momentum into Sunday's road trip to Arizona.

article.title: Blue Jays Sign Taira to Five-Year Deal
paragraphs: The Blue Jays made the biggest move of Toronto's offseason, signing Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira to a five-year, $80 million contract. Taira is expected to join the rotation, with his first scheduled Toronto game set for March 25 at Yankee Stadium. The Leafs visit Boston Friday at 1:00 p.m. on TSN, with Kirill Marchenko expected back after missing 12 games. Coach Jim Hiller's handling of Gavin McKenna's ice time remains a talking point.

The Raptors host the Nets Friday at 7:30 p.m. Toronto enters at 6-11, while Jakob Poeltl and Collin Murray-Boyles are preaching patience as the team works through its early-season struggles. The Commanders, 4-5-1 and second in the NFC East, visit Arizona Sunday at 4:25 p.m. on Fox. Jayden Daniels says he and Brandon Aiyuk have put the past behind them. For the Jays, the next date is March 25 at 1:35 p.m. ET in New York.
